physical_mismatches.reason: Nanoscale device-level 3-D FEM (183x145 nm^2 NAND gate, 1.4 um stack) differs in scale from a centimeter-scale 2D floorplan with watt-level block power. It has no block floorplan and no per-block watts; heat comes from transistor I-V Joule heating at the drain and gate blocks. The scenario is not steady_2d_relevant.

Monolithic 3-D stacking: two tiers joined by 50 nm inter-tier vias, with top-tier heating far from the sink. A 2D Studio model cannot represent this vertical tier structure, which is the cause of the hotspot.
No interposer or chiplet system, and no cooling model beyond a 300 K isothermal sink face with adiabatic sides. This differs from package-level heat-sink or cooling models.

Transient behavior is a 50% duty cycle over 100 ns. The scenario has no published power time series, and the paper's transient results are shown only in figures (Figs. 6-7), not as extractable numbers.
The paper's own heat extraction (thermal junction and tungsten pillar) is a design feature, not a controller or optimizer. It is outside the scenario and cannot be reproduced in a 2D Studio runner.
No reliability model. The paper discusses reliability only qualitatively. Nanoscale conductivity reduction (Si nanowire 13 W/m/K) and quantum effects are simplified or ignored.

studio_assumptions: No Studio package or material assumptions are recorded here, because the packet has no pinned assets and no Studio bundle specification.

Dimensions and powers do not support a placement. A separate illustrative 2D placement could be constructed only if the runner has dimensions and powers; its coordinates would be generated, not paper-derived, and its temperatures could not be compared numerically to the paper's 420 K.
